newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FOREST PROFIT FROM WRIGHT INDISCIPLINE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FOREST PROFIT FROM WRIGHT INDISCIPLINE.

text.p: Norwegian Alf-Inge Haaland turned the English premier league upside down on Saturday as struggling Nottingham Forest gratefully accepted a seasonal gift from Arsenal's Ian Wright.

Under the temporary command of England defender Stuart Pearce following the resignation of manager Frank Clark this week, bottom-placed Forest seemed to heading for another defeat when Wright put Arsenal 1-0 ahead in the 64th minute.

But Haaland put Forest back on level terms within three minutes and, with Wright dismissed for violent conduct, swept in a second goal in the 89th minute to secure a 2-1 win which prevented the Londoners from returning to the top of the table.

Wright received his marching orders after an off-the-ball incident involving Croat Nicola Jerkan, his notoriously fiery temper having already surfaced in the first-half when he barged his team-mate Paul Merson in disgust after an attack broke down.

Pearce hastened Wright on his way to the dressing-room with a few sharp words, but was grateful to the Arsenal striker for giving Forest, without a league win since the first day of the season, a boost ahead of their tough Christmas programme.
"I told him he'd been a little bit silly and he basically agreed with me," said Pearce. "I'm pleased we've won the game, but we're still bottom of the table."
Arsenal remain second, two points behind Liverpool, but they are now one of seven clubs separated by just seven points.
Champions Manchester United, in particular, are running back into form, with another Norwegian, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, and Eric Cantona both scoring twice in a 5-0 home thrashing of Sunderland.
Midfielder Nicky Butt scored the other with a header and United are now in fourth position, four points behind Arsenal and six behind Liverpool.
The result also justified manager Alex Ferguson's decision to leave England midfielder David Beckham on the bench to protect him from 'burn-out' over the hectic festive period.
The only other member of the chasing pack in action on Saturday were Chelsea who were also indebted to an overseas import in a 3-1 home win over West Ham.

Italian Gianfranco Zola scored a superb individual goal to add to a double from Welsh striker Mark Hughes, shaking Chelsea out of their recent slump and keeping them on the fringe of the title race in eighth place.

Tottenham's Danish signing Allan Nielsen added to the day's continental flavour with his side's goal in the 1-1 draw with Sheffield Wednesday and only Southampton and Coventry could claim home-grown talent tipped the scales.
Coventry won 2-0 at Leicester to move out of the bottom three with two goals from Dion Dublin and Southampton did likewise with a 3-1 success against Derby.
They are replaced in the drop-zone by Middlesbrough and Blackburn, whose match was postponed because of illness in the Middlesbrough camp.
The only goalless game of the day was at Goodison Park where Leeds were involved in their third successive stalemate but extended their unbeaten league run under George Graham to five matches.
